subject: Renewal + midterm top-up: packaging options and temporary surge offset
messages:
From: Alex Morris <alex@novaclinic.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal timing and a short-term surge this quarter

Hey Chloe —

Hope you had a good weekend. We're planning our vendor budgets for Q3 and I wanted to start the renewal conversation early. Two items: 1) we expect a ~25% spike in inference usage for a 6–8 week pilot starting mid-June and 2) our renewal is up Aug 15. Can we look at options to co-term, and whether there's a short-term surge credit (or voucher) we can use so we don't overcommit at renewal?

Also attaching a short usage forecast — happy to jump on a call.

Thanks,
Alex Morris
Director, ML Platform
NovaClinic

Attachment: nova_usage_forecast_q3.csv (attachment referenced)

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morris <alex@novaclinic.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-28T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal timing and a short-term surge this quarter

Alex —

Thanks for the heads-up and the forecast. Short answer: yes — we can support a temporary surge without forcing a full uplift at renewal, and we can co-term to align your invoice cycle to Aug 15. Two paths I typically propose:

Option A — Surge buffer + monthly true-up
- Add a 6–8 week surge credit (one-off voucher) priced at discounted rate so you can absorb the pilot; unused portion can apply to next invoice.
- Keep current renewal amount and co-term at July/Aug renewal date.

Option B — Partial annualize + temporary bucket
- Annualize a modest top-up (e.g., +15%) now to cover baseline growth, plus a small temporary bucket for the 6–8 week spike.
- We offer stepped discounts for partial annualization vs full uplift.

If you want, I can send a short spreadsheet with numbers for both options and a sample amendment language for legal/procurement. Looping Ben for pricing confirmation and Irene for contract language.

Are you available for a 30-min call tomorrow at 10am PT?

Best,
Chloe Martin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.ai
Phone: (415) 555-0132

From: Procurement Team <procurement@novaclinic.com>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Alex Morris <alex@novaclinic.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal timing and a short-term surge this quarter

Hi Chloe —

Thanks for the quick reply. Couple of procurement items before we get into detailed pricing:
- We'll need explicit language that any unused surge credit can be converted to invoice credit within 90 days of the end of the pilot.
- Any partial annualization should not extend our termination window or change SLA metrics.
- Please include a separate line in the amendment showing the temporary bucket with start/end dates.

I've attached a redline SOW we use for amendments (SOW_Redline_v1).

Procurement will be on the call with Alex if we schedule.

Thanks,
J. Patel
Senior Procurement Manager
NovaClinic

Attachment: NovaClinic_SOW_Redline_v1.pdf

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-29T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal timing and a short-term surge this quarter

Team — forwarding the procurement redline and Alex's ask. Quick take before I respond:

- They want a voucher-like surge credit that can be converted to invoice credit within 90 days. That's reasonable and low risk.
- Procurement insists partial annualization must not change termination windows or SLAs. We'll need legal to confirm amendment language keeps terms intact.
- Pricing: propose two formal pricing options (A & B from my earlier email). For A, a voucher sized at 25% of their forecasted spike priced at 60% of list token rate. For B, a +15% annualization with a blended discount (10% on the incremental).

Questions for you: Ben — are those discount levels within approval? Irene — can legal/finance support the 90-day conversion clause (no auto-extend of term)? If yes I'll send the options with a sample amendment and schedule the call.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-29T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal timing and a short-term surge this quarter

Chloe — quick notes on approvals:
- Voucher at 60% of list for a one-off short pilot is approvable up to $55k without C-level signoff. Above that we need manager approval.
- +15% annualization with 10% incremental discount is fine, but we should add a usage staircase (i.e., escape hatch) that re-evaluates discounts at the next renewal if actual usage deviates >30% from forecast.
- Finance prefers the voucher to be applied as a credit toward the first post-pilot invoice rather than holding it as a separate balance. Procurement asked 90 days; we can accept 90 days but prefer 'apply to next invoice within 60 days' operationally — could compromise at 75 days.

Irene — if legal can confirm the amendment doesn't alter termination or SLAs, I'm good to proceed.

Ben

From: Chloe Martin <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morris <alex@novaclinic.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@novaclinic.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-02T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal timing and a short-term surge this quarter — proposed paths

Alex / Procurement —

Thanks for the redline and patience while we vetted internally. Below are two concrete proposals; I attached a quick spreadsheet with the line-item math (NovaClinic_Renewal_Prices_v3.xlsx) and a draft amendment callout for your legal team.

Option 1 — Surge Voucher (recommended for pilot)
- Size: voucher equivalent to 25% of your forecasted pilot usage (per the CSV).
- Price: 60% of current token list rate for usage charged against the voucher.
- Conversion: any unused voucher value may be applied as invoice credit to the next invoice up to 75 days after pilot end. (Procurement asked 90 days; we propose 75 days operational compromise.)
- Contract impact: no change to term, termination rights, or SLAs. Amendment records voucher start/end dates.

Option 2 — Partial Annualize + Temporary Bucket
- Annualize baseline by +15% (applies for remainder of term).
- Incremental discount: 10% applied to the annualized units above current baseline.
- Temporary bucket for pilot (6–8 weeks) added as a separate line item; unused portion credited at next invoice.
- We include a staircase re-evaluation clause at renewal if usage differs >30% from forecast.

Next steps:
- If Option 1 looks good, we can issue a short amendment for signature today and activate the voucher before mid-June.
- If you'd rather go with Option 2, we'll need a quick signature and we'll apply annualized billing starting next invoice.

Please let me know which path you prefer and whether Procurement accepts the 75-day conversion window. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call to finalize.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.ai

Attachments: NovaClinic_Renewal_Prices_v3.xlsx (pricing math), NovaClinic_SOW_Redline_v1.pdf (procurement redline)
